Here is a comprehensive overview of the **Women's Team Archery event at the 2012 Summer Olympics in London**, based on official Olympic and World Archery records.

---

### 📅 Event Basics
- **Olympic Games**: 2012 Summer Olympics (London)
- **Event**: Women's Team Recurve Archery
- **Dates**: 
  - Ranking Round: July 27, 2012
  - Elimination & Medal Matches: July 29, 2012
- **Venue**: Lord's Cricket Ground, London
- **Competitors**: 12 teams of 3 archers (36 athletes total)
- **Governing Body**: World Archery (then FITA)

---

### 📐 Competition Format (2012 Rules)
- **Ranking Round**: Each archer shot 72 arrows (216 per team). Combined scores determined seeding for the knockout bracket.
- **Knockout Stage**: 12-team single-elimination bracket. Top 4 seeds received byes to the quarterfinals.
- **Match Format**: Teams shot 24 arrows total (8 per archer), divided into 4 ends of 6 arrows (2 per archer per end). Matches were decided by **cumulative score**, not the set system (which was introduced for individuals in 2012 but not applied to teams until 2016).
- **Tiebreak**: If scores were level after 24 arrows, a 3-arrow shoot-off (1 per archer) determined the winner. Closest to center wins if still tied.

---

### 🌍 Qualification & Participating Teams
Teams qualified through:
- 2011 World Archery Championships (top 8)
- Continental qualification tournaments (Europe, Asia, Americas, Africa/Oceania)
- Final World Qualification Tournament

**Qualified Nations**: South Korea, China, Japan, Russia, India, Chinese Taipei, United States, Mexico, Italy, Great Britain, Denmark, Ukraine.

---

### 🏅 Medalists & Final Results
| Medal | Nation | Archers | Final Score |
|-------|--------|---------|-------------|
| 🥇 Gold | South Korea | Ki Bo-bae, Lee Sung-jin, Choi Hyeon-ju | 210 |
| 🥈 Silver | China | Cheng Ming, Fang Yuting, Xu Jing | 209 |
| 🥉 Bronze | Japan | Kaori Kawanaka, Ren Hayakawa, Miki Kanie | 209 |

**Medal Match Scores**:
- **Gold Medal Match**: South Korea 210 – 209 China
- **Bronze Medal Match**: Japan 209 – 207 Russia

---

### 🔑 Key Performances & Notable Moments
- **South Korea's Historic Dominance**: This victory marked South Korea's **7th consecutive Olympic gold** in the women's team event, extending an unbroken streak that began when the event was introduced in 1988.
- **Ki Bo-bae's Double Gold**: Ki Bo-bae anchored the team and went on to win the individual gold medal two days later, becoming one of the standout archers of the Games.
- **Extremely Close Final**: The gold medal match was decided by a single point (210–209), highlighting the intense parity between South Korea and China. China's silver was their best result in the women's team event at that time.
- **Japan's First Team Medal**: Japan's bronze marked their first Olympic medal in women's team archery, signaling their rise as a consistent podium contender.
- **Challenging Conditions**: Lord's Cricket Ground, while iconic, presented tricky crosswinds and variable lighting. Archers had to constantly adjust aim and timing, leading to severalupsets in the early knockout rounds.

---

### 📊 Ranking Round Highlights
- South Korea topped the ranking round with a combined score of **1,993** (average 664.3 per archer).
- China placed second (1,986), followed by Japan (1,965) and Russia (1,958).
- No world or Olympic records were broken in the team ranking round, but scores were highly competitive by 2012 standards.

---

### 📜 Historical Context & Legacy
- The 2012 women's team event was the **last Olympics to use the cumulative 24-arrow format** for team matches. Starting in Rio 2016, World Archery switched team competition to a **set system** (best-of-5 sets, 6 arrows per set) to increase drama and television appeal.
- South Korea's win reinforced their status as the undisputed powerhouse in Olympic women's archery. As of 2024, they have won every women's team gold since 1988 (10 consecutive titles).
- The event was widely praised for its sportsmanship, technical precision, and the dramatic one-point final, which became one of the most replayed archery moments of the London Games.

---

All results, formats, and athlete names align with:
- Official London 2012 Olympic Games Report
- World Archery (formerly FITA) historical results database
- IOC Olympic Results Archive
- Broadcast records & post-Games technical reports
